narrative.title: The Beacon Code Counter
narrative.scenario: A lighthouse emits a long pulse string, and the coast guard hunts for one short distress code as a subsequence of those pulses. Multiple flashes can serve the same slot, so the same code may hide in the beam log many different ways. The monitoring console counts every distinct embedding of the code in the log.
narrative.inputFormat: Two strings s (the log) and t (the code).
narrative.outputFormat: Return the number of distinct subsequences of s that equal t.

testCases.explanation: Any one of the three 'b's in the log can be dropped while spelling "rabbit".
Five distinct position combinations spell "bag" in order.

hintLevels: Level 1: On a character match you may spend the log letter on the code or skip it — both branches count.
Level 2: On a match count[i][j] = count[i-1][j-1] + count[i-1][j]; on a miss just count[i-1][j]. An empty code counts exactly once.
Level 3: A 1D array swept left-to-right per log character keeps memory at the code's length.
